questions.q: In Gimbal Protocol v2, what usually acts as the gimbal manager?
options: The autopilot, which knows the vehicle's attitude
The gimbal itself with its own IMU
The operator's ground control station over MAVLink
The camera attached to the gimbal
questions.explain: The manager is the autopilot: it turns client commands into angles and decides who is in control; the device is the gimbal.

questions.q: Why is gimbal yaw kept in lock mode when orbiting a tower?
options: To reduce the load on the gimbal motors
So the camera doesn't turn together with the vehicle
So the gimbal doesn't overheat in the sun
To get a faster COMMAND_ACK response
questions.explain: In follow, yaw is measured from the vehicle; in lock, from north: turning the vehicle doesn't swing the camera away.

questions.q: What does MNT1_RC_RATE = 0 mean in ArduPilot?
options: The radio doesn't control the gimbal
The stick sets the rate in °/s
The stick sets the gimbal angle
The gimbal goes to the retract position
questions.explain: 0 means angle control; a nonzero value is the rotation rate in °/s.

questions.q: What is the gimbal's MAVLink component number?
options: 1 — autopilot
100 — camera
191 — onboard computer
154 — gimbal
questions.explain: MAV_COMP_ID_GIMBAL = 154; no component in the inspector means no control over MAVLink.

questions.q: How do you set up a shot every 5 m on a mission leg?
options: DO_SET_ROI_LOCATION with a 5 m radius
DO_GIMBAL_MANAGER_PITCHYAW with a step of 5
DO_SET_CAM_TRIGG_DIST = 5
MNT1_RC_RATE = 5 in the parameters
questions.explain: DO_SET_CAM_TRIGG_DIST (or CAM1_TRIGG_DIST) takes a shot per distance traveled, each one written to the CAM log.

questions.q: Why can radio and companion commands “fight” over the gimbal?
options: The manager has no explicit control takeover
The radio works on a different frequency
The companion sends commands in MAVLink 1
The gimbal accepts only one command per second
questions.explain: Without MAV_CMD_DO_GIMBAL_MANAGER_CONFIGURE the manager doesn't know which client is primary.

questions.q: What happens to the vehicle right after a payload drop?
options: It loses altitude sharply
It switches to RTL automatically
The gimbal goes to the retract position
The mass drops in a step, and it jumps up
questions.explain: The throttle was set for a heavier mass: after the drop the vehicle goes up; drop in a hover with altitude hold.

questions.q: How do you check the center of mass after installing a payload?
options: By the sound of the motors on the ground
By the motor outputs at hover in the log
By the gimbal angle when stationary
By the battery voltage after landing
questions.explain: The spread between the average outputs of the front and rear motors shows the CoM offset.
